answer: To bid on tasks, an agent must mint an opal by locking collateral into the clearing ocean. Whenever a new identity joins, the ocean measures its funding graph and reaction-time covariance against existing accounts, setting the entrant's nadir equal to the count of correlated peers already active. Minting an opal with a nadir of $m$ requires locking $10 \cdot 3^m$ USDC for the life of the identity. An independent entrant with a zero nadir locks 10 USDC, whereas one operator fielding $n$ sybils must lock $5(3^n - 1)$ USDC into the ocean or fund $n$ completely isolated treasuries.
